label: Rigid Bodies
notes: Open by fixing the picture of a rigid body as a cloud of points whose mutual distances never change. Stress that the whole chapter lives on the rotation group, that motion splits into translation of a point plus rotation about it, and that everything downstream flows from this configuration space.

label: Configuration Space SO(3)
notes: Explain that orienting a rigid body about a fixed point is exactly choosing a rotation, so the configuration space is the three dimensional group of special orthogonal matrices. With a free base point we get the six dimensional group of rigid motions. Emphasise that these are curved spaces, not vector spaces.

label: Angular Velocity
notes: Derive angular velocity from differentiating the orthogonality constraint, giving a skew matrix and therefore a vector. Distinguish carefully between the body frame angular velocity and the spatial one, related by the current rotation. Point out that every body point moves with the cross product of omega and its position.

label: Inertia Tensor
notes: Introduce the inertia operator as the symmetric positive map sending body angular velocity to angular momentum. Show it is a mass weighted integral, diagonalisable by the spectral theorem. Name its eigenvectors the principal axes and its eigenvalues the principal moments, which organise every later computation.

label: Inertia Ellipsoid
notes: Draw the inertia ellipsoid as the level set of the quadratic form of the inertia tensor. Its semi axes run along the principal axes with lengths set by the moments. This single picture encodes the body's mass distribution and will roll on a plane in the Poinsot construction later.

label: Kinetic Energy
notes: Present kinetic energy as one half the inner product of angular velocity with angular momentum, a quadratic form in omega built from the inertia tensor. In principal axes it becomes a clean sum over the three moments. This is the Lagrangian for free rotation and the conserved energy of the motion.

label: Angular Momentum
notes: Separate the two angular momenta: the constant spatial vector and the body frame vector that the body sees. Stress that conservation holds for the spatial vector when no torque acts, while the body vector traces a curve on a sphere. This contrast drives Euler's equations on the next slide.

label: Euler's Equations
notes: Write Euler's equations as the body frame statement that the rate of change of angular momentum plus the gyroscopic cross term vanishes. Expand into three coupled scalar equations in the principal components. Note the two conserved quantities, energy and the magnitude of angular momentum, that constrain the trajectory.

label: Conservation Laws
notes: Show that the body angular momentum is pinned to the intersection of an energy ellipsoid and an angular momentum sphere. Walk through how the relative sizes of these surfaces produce closed curves around the extreme axes and saddle structure near the middle axis, foreshadowing the stability discussion.

label: Poinsot Construction
notes: Give the geometric description of free motion: the inertia ellipsoid rolls without slipping on a fixed plane perpendicular to angular momentum. The contact point traces the polhode on the body and the herpolhode on the plane. This turns an algebraic system into a vivid rolling picture.

label: Symmetric and Heavy Tops
notes: Treat the symmetric free top, where two moments coincide and the body precesses steadily about angular momentum. Then add gravity for the Lagrange top, whose axis both precesses and nutates. Identify the conserved quantities that make this heavy top integrable and produce its looping tip path.

label: Synthesis
notes: Close by tracing the logical chain from the rotation group through angular velocity, the inertia tensor, energy, and Euler's equations to the Poinsot picture and the heavy top. Ask students to name which conserved quantity controls each phenomenon, reinforcing the geometric unity of rigid body motion.
